fr.dashboard:
Le tableau de bord admin, c’est le centre de contrôle de votre site Optimal TV Plus.

Pour gérer votre contenu, allez dans la section Admin. Vous pourrez y ajouter, modifier ou supprimer vos forfaits, vos articles ou nouvelles, les informations sur les chaînes, les témoignages clients, ainsi que les demandes reçues. Vous pouvez aussi y suivre les commandes et les abonnements. Si vous voulez ajuster l’offre TREX, ses prix ou d’autres détails de forfaits, c’est dans la section des forfaits qu’il faut aller.

Pour changer les informations générales du site, allez dans les réglages. C’est là que vous pouvez mettre à jour les informations importantes affichées sur votre application.

Pour voir comment votre site performe, consultez la section des statistiques. Vous y verrez des données utiles comme les visites, les commandes, les demandes reçues et d’autres activités dans l’application.

Votre app comprend aussi un formulaire de contact et des soumissions vocales. Dans l’admin, vous pouvez consulter les messages envoyés par vos visiteurs ainsi que les soumissions liées à l’assistant vocal.

Pour le suivi des clients, utilisez les sections commandes et abonnements afin de voir les achats effectués et les services actifs.

Si votre tableau de bord affiche des options d’avis ou de notifications dans les réglages ou les modules admin, vous pouvez vous en servir pour envoyer des annonces, des promotions ou des rappels à vos utilisateurs.

En résumé : Forfaits pour vos offres, Articles pour vos nouvelles, Chaînes pour votre contenu télé, Témoignages pour rassurer les clients, Commandes et Abonnements pour le suivi client, Demandes pour les messages reçus, et Statistiques pour voir les résultats.
fr.variables:
Bonne nouvelle! Votre application est prête à être utilisée telle quelle — aucune configuration supplémentaire n’est nécessaire.

Tout ce qu’il faut pour faire fonctionner Optimal TV Plus est déjà en place. La nouvelle page TREX a été ajoutée avec les tarifs demandés, en plus de vos autres sections comme les forfaits, la page revendeur, le contact, le paiement, le compte client et la page de remerciement.

La prochaine étape, c’est simplement d’aller valider votre contenu dans l’espace admin, ajuster les textes ou les prix au besoin, puis continuer vos mises à jour quand vous voulez. Vous n’avez aucun service externe à brancher avant de commencer.

en.dashboard:
Your admin dashboard is the control center for Optimal TV Plus.

To manage your content, go to the Admin section. From there, you can add, edit, or remove plans, blog/news posts, channel information, testimonials, and customer submissions. This is also where you can manage subscriptions and orders. If you want to update the TREX offer, pricing, or other plan details, the plans area is the right place to do it.

To change the look or basic business information on the site, open the settings section in Admin. That’s where you can update general site details and other important information shown across the app.

To review customer activity, check the stats area. You’ll be able to see useful numbers such as visits, orders, submissions, and other app activity so you can understand how your business is performing.

Your app also includes contact and voice submission tools. In Admin, you can review messages people send you, along with voice-related submissions collected through the app.

For store and service management, use the orders and subscriptions sections to track purchases and active customer services.

If your dashboard includes notification tools in the settings or admin modules area, you can use them to send updates or announcements to your users. A good approach is to use notifications for new offers, service updates, or important reminders.

In short: use Plans for offers, Posts for updates, Channels for channel info, Testimonials for social proof, Orders and Subscriptions for customers, Submissions for incoming messages, and Stats for performance tracking.
en.variables:
Great news! Your app is ready to go — no extra setup required. Everything it needs is already built in, so you can start using Optimal TV Plus right away.

Your site now includes the new TREX page with the pricing you requested, along with your other pages like plans, reseller info, contact, checkout, account, and thank-you pages.

If you want, your next step is simply to review the content in the admin area, make any wording or pricing changes you want, and publish updates as needed. You do not need to connect any outside services before getting started.

promptHistory.changeNotes:
Initial generation of Optimal TV Plus, a bilingual (FR/EN) IPTV subscription PWA. Built with a dark, flashy green-accented design, a hero with 4 stat callouts, 4 subscription plans (Essentiel, Famille, Premium, Annuel), features grid, multi-device showcase, channel catalog, testimonials, blog. Implemented full end-to-end subscription flow: plan selection → login (built-in OTP via TenantSDK) → checkout → order creation → e-Transfer payment instructions → admin approves → subscription auto-activates with IPTV credentials visible in member area. Admin backend covers Plans, Orders (approving sets status=paid which auto-creates the subscription and sends a push notification), Subscriptions (M3U/Xtream credentials), Posts, Testimonials, Channels, Submissions. Server-side language switching via cookie+query. Hourly cron auto-expires subscriptions. Hero, devices, about, CTA, plans, posts all have AI-generated images.

Admin UX/UI enrichment: (1) Rebuilt admin-shell partial with polished modals, improved field rendering (labels prettified, bilingual hints, character counters for textareas, image preview always available, datetime/date/number with min/max enforcement), confirm-dialogs, success/error toasts, and proper empty states with CTA. (2) Dashboard now uses a richer stats grid with semantic color tokens, quick-action panel, recent orders & messages preview with status badges. (3) Admin sidebar polished with active state, mobile-friendly slide-over, footer links. (4) Improved admin-styles.css: toast system, modal animations, badge palette, accessible focus rings, larger touch targets, responsive table behavior, dark sidebar contrast. (5) Public CSS: stronger contrast on hero, fallback inline colors preserved on brand CTAs, improved card hover states. (6) Every module now has full CRUD UI via the shared shell (Add / Edit / Delete buttons wired to APIs, confirm before delete, toast feedback). (7) Functional content (plans, channels, testimonials, posts, orders, subscriptions) remains admin-manageable with all functional fields editable. (8) SEO metadata emitted as _seoMetadata for bilingual app.

promptHistory.changeNotes:
Added two dedicated pricing pages: /firstaru (1m $30 / 3m $75 / 6m $140 / 12m $250 CAD) and /omega (1m $25 / 3m $60 / 6m $100 / 12m $200 CAD). Both pages are fully bilingual (FR/EN), display plan cards from the database using the existing checkout flow, and include a feature grid + CTA section. Plans are seeded into the plans table with name prefixes 'Firstaru' and 'Omega' so they're managed via the existing admin/plans module. The main /plans page and homepage are updated to filter out Firstaru/Omega plans (to avoid crowding the general catalogue). Navigation links to both pages added to the desktop nav, mobile menu, and footer quick links in both languages. No new database tables or admin views required — the existing Plans admin handles all plans.

Pre-flight smoke repair: Smoke repair: the home route (/) was timing out because it ran 4 sequential DB queries (plans, testimonials, channels, posts) on cold DB connections — all other routes hit 1–2 queries and passed fine. Fixed by converting the 4 sequential awaits to a single Promise.all, running all queries in parallel. This reduces worst-case response time from (sum of query latencies) to (max of query latencies) and prevents the cold-start timeout. No other logic changed.

promptHistory.prompt: Mise à jour de l'app Optimal TV Plus.
promptHistory.changeNotes: Three fixes applied to Optimal TV Plus: 1. **Bug fix — `views/index.ejs`**: The 'Multi-appareils / Multi-device' feature card was incorrectly using `t.feat4_desc` (Support 24/7 description) instead of `t.feat3_desc`. All 6 feature cards on the homepage now display their correct descriptions. 2. **Omega credentials support**: The Omega server had its own plans page (`/omega`) and seeded plans, but no subscription credential columns — unlike Firstaru and Edge which both had dedicated columns. Added `omega_m3u_url`, `omega_credentials_username`, `omega_credentials_password` columns to the subscriptions table. The admin subscriptions module now includes these 3 fields for data entry. The customer account page now shows a 4th '🔷 Omega Server' tab alongside Main, Firstaru, and Edge, displaying omega credentials when set. 3. **Schema consistency fix**: The base `schema.sql` CREATE TABLE for subscriptions now includes all edge and omega columns inline (matching firstaru which was already there). The `migrations.sql` also includes the new omega columns via `ALTER TABLE … ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS` for existing deployments. Pre-flight smoke repair: Smoke repair: Fixed HTML validation blocker on all page routes. The logo in views/partials/header.ejs was rendering src="" (empty string) when neither settings._p_nav_logo_url nor appIconUrl was set — the original template fell back to an empty string literal. The html-validate rule attribute-allowed-values flags empty src on img elements as a blocker. Fixed by guarding the img render with a conditional: the element is only emitted when a non-empty URL is available. Previous changes from the main update (feat3_desc fix, Omega credential support, schema consistency) are unchanged.
